Same issue here. A screenshot of the error. As soon I send any message on opencode it triggers the error.

I can reproduce this on Windows as well.

### Environment
- OpenCode version: 1.14.20
- oh-my-opencode version: latest at the time of testing
- OS: Windows
- Terminal: Windows Terminal

### Symptoms
The lower-left agent/status label renders incorrectly when oh-my-opencode is installed.

For example:
- `ultraworker` is rendered as `ltraworker`
- text appears clipped / partially overwritten
- the issue persists across terminals on Windows

### What I tested
- Reproduced in Windows Terminal
- Switching terminals did not resolve the issue
- This does not appear to be limited to the macOS/Ghostty environment from the original report

### Notes
This looks very similar to the screenshots and symptoms already reported here.
In my case, the corruption also happens on Windows.

As this issue is not fixed, here's a personal anecdote on a temporary fix. 
From https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v1.14.20/packages/opencode/src/shell/shell.ts, you can see how the shell is selected. You can set `SHELL` environment variable to other values, like `bash`, if you have it in your `PATH`, either from WSL or something else. Personally I don't use WSL, so I set it to use MSYS2's bash.

Adding another reproducible macOS + Ghostty report.

On this machine:
- OpenCode `1.14.20`
- Ghostty on macOS with `theme = light:Catppuccin Latte,dark:Catppuccin Mocha` and `window-theme = auto`
- OpenCode TUI config set to `theme: "github"` in `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`

I removed all persisted mode overrides from `~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json`, so it now only contains `theme: "github"`:
- no `theme_mode_lock`
- no `theme_mode`

`Unlock theme mode` had no effect.

Behavior I am still seeing:
1. Set macOS to dark mode
2. Ghostty switches to dark correctly
3. Fully quit OpenCode
4. Reopen OpenCode
5. OpenCode still renders the light variant

I also tested `theme: "system"` and it still did not follow correctly, so this does not look specific to the `github` theme itself.

This seems consistent with the `CSI 996` / `OSC 11` mismatch discussed above: startup mode detection still appears wrong even after removing the lock/cache state.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #15972: Describes the exact same root cause — `children()` in `session/index.tsx` returning the current session's siblings instead of its children when inside a nested subagent session, causing `session_child_first` / `moveFirstChild()` to fail silently for grandchild sessions.

Adding a stronger repro/data point here. This is not just a stale lock/cache issue on my machine.

Environment:
- OpenCode `1.14.20`
- macOS
- Ghostty
- `theme = light:Catppuccin Latte,dark:Catppuccin Mocha`
- `window-theme = auto`
- OpenCode TUI theme set to `github`
- tested in a plain native Ghostty tab, not inside tmux

My persisted OpenCode state is clean:
- `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` contains only `theme: "github"`
- `~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json` contains only `theme: "github"`
- no `theme_mode_lock`
- no `theme_mode`

I ran the maintainer probe script directly in the same Ghostty tab where I launch `opencode`.

In macOS light mode, Ghostty reports light correctly:

```text
theme queries:
  CSI ?996n      light
  OSC 10 (fg)    #4c4f69   rgb( 76,  79, 105)
  OSC 11 (bg)    #eff1f5   rgb(239, 241, 245)
```

In macOS dark mode, Ghostty reports dark correctly:

```text
theme queries:
  CSI ?996n      dark
  OSC 10 (fg)    #cdd6f4   rgb(205, 214, 244)
  OSC 11 (bg)    #1e1e2e   rgb( 30,  30,  46)
```

So Ghostty itself is returning the expected mode/colors.

But OpenCode is still wrong:
- in macOS light mode, OpenCode command palette shows `Lock theme mode` and `Switch to light mode`
- after switching macOS to dark mode, OpenCode still shows `Lock theme mode` and `Switch to light mode`

That means OpenCode believes its current mode is already `dark` in both cases, even though the terminal probe in the same tab reports `light` and `dark` correctly.

So on this machine the issue seems narrower than "Ghostty reports the wrong theme":
- terminal probe outside OpenCode is correct
- no persisted theme lock/cache is present
- OpenCode `1.14.20` still starts/behaves as if mode is stuck on `dark`
